changes: Fresh init now writes Lattice-named assets by default: LATTICE.md, bin/lattice.js, bin/lattice-codex.js, and .Codex/lattice.json. Legacy Koala assets remain recognized for existing projects. Runtime diagnostics now prefer lattice, fall back to koala, and detect project-local lattice shadowing.
usage: Run lattice init for new projects. New projects should use Lattice local files and wrappers. Existing projects with KOALA.md, bin/koala*.js, or .Codex/koala.json continue to pass compatibility checks and can migrate gradually.
expectedOutcome: A new project initialized by Lattice should not receive duplicate Koala-named generated files, while old Koala projects should still verify and operate through compatibility paths.
actualTranscript: validate --story=B-b95c --json passed with 12/12 verification intents covered. lattice-branded-init, legacy-koala-compatibility, validation-protocol, runtime-fact-contract, and verify_codex passed; verify_codex had only a non-hard global fallback advisory.
outcomeDiff: Expected and actual match. Lattice is primary for new generated assets; Koala remains a legacy alias and compatibility surface. The only advisory is global fallback pointing at another worktree, which is not current-worktree gate evidence.
limitations: Global fallback CLI may point at another worktree and is reported as heartbeat-only advisory; this story did not change package names or external authority semantics.
pitfalls: Avoid parallel finding_resolve commands because they can race on the Git index lock. Keep unrelated prompt/background wording churn stashed so review evaluates the actual committed story scope.
